title: The Day That Outlasts the Year

beats.narration: On Venus, a single day lasts longer than the entire year.
Venus takes 243 Earth days to spin once — but only 225 to circle the Sun.
Watch the race. Venus finishes a full lap of the Sun before it completes a single turn.
On Earth the math is friendly: one spin, one day. One orbit, one year.
Venus also spins backwards — so its sun climbs out of the west and sets in the east.
Count sunrise to sunrise, and a Venus day stretches to 117 Earth days. A whole year passes between barely two dawns.
Why so slow? Nobody knows for sure. An ancient collision may have flipped it — or its own crushing atmosphere dragged it to a crawl.
On Venus, the year always wins.
